sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Kumar Singh,P.K. Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Dewarshi Kumar Rai, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasia,
learned State Law Officer for the State and also perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 158 of 2024 under Sections 376, 452 I.P.C. Police Station Muskara, District Hamirpur during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant along with two other co-accused persons are stated to have climbed to the terrace of the informant's house in inebriated state in the night of 28.04.2024 at about 02:00 AM and committed rape with the daughter of the informant.

Mahesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180732349/
1 5.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by about two months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
There is no medical corroboration of the incident.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant further stated that even her vital body parts were found intact,
as such, there is no possibility of her being subjected to any kind of sexual assault.
It is a clear cut case of false implication.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 06.07.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant- Mahesh, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
